post.caption:
A laser is coherent light: one wavelength, one direction, every wave in step. That is why the beam barely spreads, which makes it a precision tool rather than just a bright light. Fibre communication, barcode scanners, eye surgery and metal cutting all depend on it. The standout is lunar ranging: Apollo crews left retroreflectors on the Moon, and timing a laser's return measures the distance to millimetres. That is how we know the Moon drifts about 3.8 cm further away each year.
